findings.issue_text: **1. `packages/core/EventManager.ts:119` - unguarded property access crashes every Google Meet booking without a destination calendar.**

`mainHostDestinationCalendar` is `undefined` whenever `destinationCalendar` is `null` or `[]` - exactly the state `handleNewBooking.ts:1063-1067` produces when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar. The old code used `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`, which returned `undefined` and correctly fell through to the Cal Video fallback. Now `create()` throws `TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading 'integration')` and the whole booking fails.
**2. `packages/core/EventManager.ts:207-208` - `updateLocation` now writes booking references with `externalCalendarId: undefined` and `credentialId: undefined`.**

These results come from `updateAllCalendarEvents` -> `CalendarManager.updateEvent`, and `updateEvent` (`packages/core/CalendarManager.ts:313-323`) returns **neither** `externalId` **nor** `credentialId` - only `createEvent` was extended. The previous code fell back to `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId` / `?.credentialId`, so it produced real values.

*Failure scenario:* organizer edits a booking's location -> `editLocation.handler.ts:113-123` creates `BookingReference` rows with `externalCalendarId = null, credentialId = null`. Any later update or cancellation takes the legacy branch and targets `"primary"` (`googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:321`) instead of the actual calendar.
**3. `packages/core/EventManager.ts:170` - non-calendar (video) references lose their `credentialId`.**
**4. `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:254-256` and `:314-316` - self-defeating `find` predicate makes the fallback dead code.**
**5. `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/organizations/create.handler.ts:151,153` - unrelated logic inversion.**
...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug }),
...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { requestedSlug: slug }),
**6. `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:1077-1079` - the feature silently no-ops when the organizer has no destination calendar.**
**7. `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:987-1079` - no de-duplication of destination calendars.**
**8. `office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:73`, `larkcalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts:128`, `packages/lib/CalendarService.ts:156` - only Google honours the per-credential destination.**

*Failure scenario:* collective event with two Office 365 hosts. The loop calls host B's O365 service, which builds `/me/calendars/<host A's externalId>/events` with host B's token -> 404/403; the 404 swallow in `CalendarManager.ts:239` makes it fail silently with no reference and no surfaced error.
**9. `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:443-464` - recurring cancellation is quadratic and still single-calendar.**
**10. `packages/core/EventManager.ts:169` - `externalCalendarId` lost for destinations without a `credentialId`.**
**11. `packages/core/EventManager.ts:591-595` - error logging removed, `message` left as dead code.**
**12. `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:724-761` - `loadUsers` rewrite is unrelated, drops a select, and flattens error types.**

The dynamic-booking branch lost `organization: { select: { slug: true } }`. `IsFixedAwareUser` (line 352) declares `organization: { slug: string }` as required and the code casts at line 870, so the compiler won't catch it; `getBookerUrl(organizerUser)` and any org-slug consumer sees `undefined` for dynamic group bookings.
The `catch` converts every non-Prisma, non-HttpError failure into a generic `500 "Unable to load users"`, discarding message and stack on the booking hot path.
`throw new Error("dynamicUserList is not properly defined or empty.")` is caught by its own `catch` and re-thrown as a 500, not the 400 it wants to be.
None of this relates to destination calendars; it belongs in a separate PR.

`destinationCalendar` in webhook payloads is now an array (`apps/web/playwright/webhook.e2e.ts:249`) for some paths but still `null` for others (lines 119, 373; `handleNewBooking.ts:1067`). External consumers parsing this field break, and the empty representation is inconsistent (`null` from `handleNewBooking`, `[]` from `confirm.handler`, the payment webhooks and the reminder cron). Pick one (prefer `[]`) and note the payload change in docs/changelog.

**15. `packages/core/EventManager.ts:341-380` and `:502-525` - the ~20-line DB credential-fetch block is duplicated verbatim** (a third near-copy is in `handleCancelBooking.ts:430-439`). Extract a `getCredentialForDestination(credentialId)` helper. Note the `handleCancelBooking` copy omits the `app: { select: { slug: true } }` include the other two rely on.

**16. `packages/core/EventManager.ts:337` - sequential `await` inside `for (const destination of ...)`.** A 5-host collective event serialises 5 Google API round-trips plus up to 5 credential lookups on the synchronous booking request. Consider `Promise.all` over destinations and a single batched `findMany({ where: { id: { in: ids } } })`.

**17. `packages/core/EventManager.ts:355-357, 373` - silent failure paths.** If the credential is missing from both memory and DB, or `credentialFromDB.app?.slug` is null, the destination is skipped with no log and no `success: false` result, so the booking reports success while one host's calendar was never written.

**18. `handleNewBooking.ts:990-1006` - collecting `teamDestinationCalendars` as a side effect of the `teamMemberPromises` map.** It happens to be safe (the push runs synchronously before the first `await`), but a future reordering that moves the push after an `await` would silently drop calendars. Use a separate `users.slice(1)` filter/map.

**19. `handleNewBooking.ts:998-999` - `firstName: ""`, `lastName: ""` added to team member objects.** Unexplained by the PR intent; if any email template prefers `firstName` over `name`, team members render with blank names.

**20. `packages/types/Calendar.d.ts:182` - `schedulingType?: SchedulingType | null` added to `CalendarEvent`** and set in `handleNewBooking.ts:1075`, but never read. Either use it (e.g. drive the collective fan-out inside `EventManager`, which is cleaner layering) or drop it.

**21. `handleNewBooking.ts:1874-1879` - only `destinationCalendar[0]` is persisted onto the `Booking` row.** Reasonable given the scalar `destinationCalendarId` relation, but the booking record no longer describes where the event actually lives. Worth a comment and eventually a join table.

**22. `handleCancelBooking.ts:436` - the DB-fetched credential is assigned to a variable inferred from `bookingToDelete.user.credentials`.** If that Prisma select is narrowed later this becomes a type error or shape mismatch; type it explicitly as `CredentialPayload`.

**9. `packages/features/bookings/lib/handleCancelBooking.ts:443-464` - recurring cancellation is quadratic and still single-calendar.**

adjudication.rationale: Real issue. In the recurring-cancellation branch in `handleCancelBooking.ts`, the code still does `const bookingRef = updBooking.references.find((ref) => ref.type.includes("_calendar"));` (not `filter`), so if each booking now has multiple calendar references (as the diff elsewhere changes destinationCalendar/references to arrays), it will only delete the *first* calendar event per updated booking (“still single-calendar”). Also, the diff adds an outer loop over `bookingCalendarReference` (now an array) while keeping the existing nested loops over `user.credentials.filter(..._calendar)` and then `for (const updBooking of updatedBookings)`, making the work multiplicative across references * credentials * updatedBookings (i.e., worse-than-linear; “quadratic” in the common case where updatedBookings grows with series size).

adjudication_records.issue_text: **10. `packages/core/EventManager.ts:169` - `externalCalendarId` lost for destinations without a `credentialId`.**

adjudication.rationale: Real issue. In `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, when a destination has no `credentialId`, it calls `createEvent(c, event)` (no third arg), so `CalendarManager.createEvent` returns an `EventResult` with `externalId` undefined (it only echoes the passed `externalId`). Later in `EventManager` (around the referenced line), `externalCalendarId` is now set from `result.externalId` instead of `evt.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. That means for destinations without `credentialId`, the created booking reference will lose `externalCalendarId` (be undefined), which can break later update/delete operations that rely on `externalCalendarId` to target the correct calendar.

adjudication.rationale: In `EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents`, when iterating `for (const destination of event.destinationCalendar)`, the code tries to find a matching credential in memory, and if not found, fetches from DB. The subsequent `if (credential) { ... createdEvents.push(...) }` block is then skipped, and because `destination.credentialId` was truthy, the `else` branch (which would try matching by integration type) is not executed either. There is no log, no error propagation, and no `success:false` `EventResult` pushed for that destination, so that destination calendar write is silently dropped. This is directly visible in the diff around the new credential-fetching logic in `createAllCalendarEvents`.
